FCDO Foreign travel advice: Saudi Arabia. PRIMARY SOURCE, approved (gov.uk).

"Your travel insurance could be invalidated if you travel against advice from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)."

AREAS WHERE FCDO ADVISES AGAINST TRAVEL - FCDO advises against:
- all travel to within 10km of the border with Yemen
- all but essential travel to Aseer province, Riyadh province, Najran province, Jizan province and the cities of Taif, Jeddah and Dammam
- all but essential travel to ALL AIRPORTS WITHIN SAUDI ARABIA EXCEPT FOR MEDINA INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT

"As an alternative to airports within Saudi Arabia, British Nationals wishing to depart Saudi Arabia should consider options to travel by land to one of the following countries and fly from there" - Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, Jordan.

REGIONAL TENSIONS section:
"Following a serious incident at King Khalid International Airport on 10 October 2026 at approximately 1500 (local time), we advise British nationals to avoid King Khalid International Airport until the airport is secure and to monitor the advice of the Saudi authorities."
"Since 13 July, the Houthis (a military group in Yemen) have launched missiles and drones targeting several locations in Saudi Arabia. There is a heightened threat against airports, military bases, ports and energy infrastructure across Saudi Arabia, including Abha, Jizan, Najran, Riyadh, Jeddah and Yanbu, as well as shipping in the Red Sea. FURTHER ATTACKS AGAINST AIRPORTS ARE VERY LIKELY. Follow Saudi Civil Defence alerts."
Advice to British nationals: if travelling by road to a neighbouring country check entry requirements; vehicle must be wholly owned and registered in your name; carry emergency supplies and essential medication; "Travel within or out of Saudi Arabia is at your own risk."
"British nationals currently in the Middle East should be prepared for possible flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruption" - refrain from capturing or sharing images of conflict-related incidents; stay away from areas around oil infrastructure and military facilities; exercise caution at transport hubs; if advised to take shelter, "an interior stairwell or a room with as few external walls or windows as possible may provide additional protection. The greatest risk is from falling debris caused by intercepts."
"The US and Iran announced a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on 17 June 2026 in relation to the conflict in the Middle East, however the situation in the Middle East remains unpredictable."
